chunks: From al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali, from Abu Basir, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: Do not eat from the slaughtered meat of the Magians.
And he said: Do not eat the slaughtered meat of the Christians of Taghlib, for they are the polytheists of the Arabs.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating the meat of Magians and Christians of Taghlib according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the Magians (Zoroastrians), whose meat is generally prohibited, and the Christians of Taghlib, who are specifically classified as polytheists (*Mushrikun*) due to their unique theological stance, making their meat impermissible. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential nuance that not all 'People of the Book' are treated identically, particularly when a group exhibits distinct polytheistic characteristics or tribal identity. The reference to Taghlib underscores the historical context of early Islamic Arabia, where certain Christian tribes were viewed as having deviated from strict monotheism.
